seoTitle: How to Put an Image in a Notion Table or Database
metaDescription: Add images directly inside a Notion table or database for product catalogs, mood boards, or project tracking with visuals alongside your data.
intro: Text-only rows can make a Notion database hard to scan, especially for things like product catalogs or mood boards where a quick visual matters. This guide covers how to add an image property to a Notion table so every row can carry a picture along with its text and other properties.

steps.heading: Add a Files & Media property
steps.body: Open your Notion table and add a new column set to the Files & Media property type — this is what lets each row hold an image.

steps.heading: Upload or link an image per row
steps.body: Click into the new property on a row and either upload an image file directly or paste an image URL to attach it.

steps.heading: Adjust how images display
steps.body: Depending on the view, you can preview the image inline in the table or open it larger by clicking the entry.

steps.heading: Organize images across the database
steps.body: Keep image sizes and formats consistent across rows so your table stays visually tidy as it grows.

faq.question: Can I add more than one image per row?
faq.answer: Yes, the Files & Media property accepts multiple uploads in a single cell, so you can attach several images to one entry.

faq.question: Does adding images slow down my Notion database?
faq.answer: Large databases with many high-resolution images can load a bit slower, so it helps to keep image file sizes reasonable.

faq.question: Can I use images from a URL instead of uploading?
faq.answer: Yes, you can paste a direct image link instead of uploading a file, which keeps your Notion storage usage lower.

faq.question: Will the image show up in gallery or board views too?
faq.answer: Yes, once you set an image property as the card cover, it will display in gallery and board views as well as the table.
